questions.q:
A furniture designer is to develop a cabinet.

Which factor should be considered first?
options: The tools available
The needs of the client
The time frame of the project
The selling price of the cabinet
questions.explanation: The design process begins with a needs analysis: the designer must first establish what the client requires before tools, scheduling or cost can be meaningfully addressed. These other factors are constraints that follow once the need is defined.

questions.q:
An architect has been contracted to design a beach resort.

Which of the following would be the most appropriate method for the architect to communicate their initial design ideas to the client?
options: A prototype
A written report
A rendered sketch
A technical diagram
questions.explanation: At the initial ideation stage a rendered sketch quickly and visually conveys the look and feel of a concept to a client. Prototypes and technical diagrams belong to later, more developed stages of the design process.

questions.q:
A project team is conducting a needs analysis for a design project.

During the needs analysis, the team will
options: identify opportunities.
develop financial plans.
formulate a time and action plan.
establish criteria for material selection.
questions.explanation: A needs analysis explores the problem and identifies opportunities and the needs to be met. Financial plans, time and action plans, and material-selection criteria are developed later, once the need has been clarified.

questions.q:
A designer has created an integrated home security system.

Which strategy would best evaluate its ease of use?
options: Trial the system in different households
Analyse the choice of manufacturing materials
Seek feedback from a large group of technicians
Conduct market research on its likely acceptance
questions.explanation: Ease of use is best evaluated by trialling the system with real end users in authentic settings, providing direct feedback on usability. Material analysis, technician feedback and market acceptance measure other attributes, not everyday usability.

questions.q:
A manufacturer wishes to decrease the long-term environmental impact of the washing machine it produces.

Which of the following strategies would be the most effective?
options: Replace plastic parts with metal where possible
Reduce the power and water usage requirements
Reduce the size of the washing bowl and detergent container
Manufacture the washing machine using only new technologies
questions.explanation: Over a washing machine's long service life, the resources it consumes in use dominate its environmental footprint, so reducing power and water use gives the greatest long-term benefit. Swapping materials or shrinking components has far less impact.

questions.q: A design company acts ethically when it
options: ensures that entrepreneurs invest in their designs.
enables the user to purchase goods for their intended use.
enables the consumer to enjoy the product and know it will minimise harm.
uses technologically advanced production processes and renewable resources.
questions.explanation: Ethical design centres on the wellbeing of the consumer — delivering a product that can be enjoyed while minimising harm to the user and others. The other options describe commercial or production choices rather than ethical responsibility.

questions.q:
A web design company has introduced a collaborative design approach.

Which of the following is likely to take place?
options: Team members multi-task in each project.
A project manager directs the development of ideas.
Each design project is allocated to all team members.
Team members work together to discuss and share ideas.
questions.explanation: Collaborative design relies on team members working together to discuss and share ideas, pooling varied expertise in cooperative decision-making. A single manager directing ideas describes a directed rather than collaborative approach.

questions.q: Life cycle analysis is a process that is most commonly used to
options: predict the duration of the different stages in a product's life.
determine the sustainability of a product once it is manufactured.
evaluate the environmental impacts at different stages of a product's life.
establish the sustainability of a product compared with similar products in the market.
questions.explanation: A life cycle analysis assesses the environmental impacts of a product at every stage, from raw-material extraction through manufacture and use to disposal. It measures impact across the whole life, not just duration or post-manufacture sustainability.

questions.q: Why do many manufacturing companies incorporate built-in obsolescence into their products?
options: To increase the probability of consistent sales
To ensure that the product is sustainable in the market place
To extend the product's life span beyond the warranty period
To make the product safe to use for an extended period of time
questions.explanation: Built-in obsolescence deliberately limits a product's lifespan so consumers must replace it, generating repeat purchases and consistent sales for the manufacturer. It works against, not towards, extended lifespan or sustainability.

questions.q: How can designers best achieve sustainable design?
options: Create designs that follow the latest trends.
Ensure that a product will be durable and competitive in the marketplace.
Seek to reduce both the negative impact of the design on the environment and the cost to the consumer.
Provide the consumer with products that are environmentally friendly and use the minimum amount of resources.
questions.explanation: Sustainable design minimises environmental harm by making products environmentally friendly and using the minimum amount of resources across their life. Durability and reducing cost help, but resource efficiency and environmental friendliness are the defining sustainable goals.

questions.q:
The images show two chairs that have been developed for different uses: an office chair and a kitchen bench stool.

How have design factors been applied differently in the development of the two chairs? Support your answer with examples.

criteria.descriptor: Shows a detailed understanding of how design factors have been applied to BOTH chairs with examples
Outlines how design factors have been applied to BOTH chairs with at least ONE example
Outlines how a design factor is applied to ONE of the chairs
Identifies a design factor of ONE chair

questions.modelAnswer: Function, ergonomics and aesthetics are applied differently to suit each chair's use. The office chair is designed for extended sitting, so ergonomic factors are prominent — adjustable height, back support and castors for movability — and it is styled for a professional, supportive look. The kitchen stool is used for shorter periods, so it has simpler ergonomics, with material and styling chosen for durability and ease of cleaning and for greater aesthetic impact in the kitchen setting.

questions.q: Why is ongoing evaluation important to a designer?

criteria.descriptor: Demonstrates why ongoing evaluation is important to a designer
Identifies an aspect of evaluation

questions.modelAnswer: Evaluation gathers information so judgements can be made about a product. Ongoing evaluation keeps that information current and relevant throughout development, allowing every element of the design to be monitored continually and adjusted so that needs are met and a quality, safe product reaches the market.

questions.q: Discuss the use of technology to conduct an evaluation of a product.

criteria.descriptor: Provides points for and/or against the use of technology to conduct evaluation of a product
Describes the use of technology to conduct evaluation of a product
Outlines the use of technology to conduct evaluation of a product
Identifies a use of technology to conduct evaluation

questions.modelAnswer: Technology lets evaluation be carried out efficiently and accurately. Using online tools and social media, surveys can be emailed or posted to consumers for immediate response, and the returned data — both qualitative and quantitative — can be collated and evaluated quickly. Because the feedback is immediate and ongoing, issues can be identified and addressed at any stage of development, though reliance on online channels can also bias the sample towards connected users.

questions.q: Explain how the development of innovative products may contribute to the quality of life.

criteria.descriptor: Provides why AND/OR how the development of innovative products contributes to the quality of life, showing clear relationship between the two
Describes how the development of innovative products contributes to the quality of life
Outlines how the development of innovative products contributes to the quality of life
Shows some understanding of innovative products and the quality of life
Shows a basic understanding of innovative products or the quality of life

questions.modelAnswer: Design seeks to satisfy needs, and innovative products improve quality of life by meeting those needs in new ways. Computer-aided and automated technologies make everyday activities faster, easier and less labour-intensive — for example timers and remote controls for lights, blinds and air-conditioning make the home more comfortable, safer and more enjoyable. Innovations in cars, such as GPS, driving cameras, Bluetooth and advanced braking and suspension, improve the safety and capability of travel. Medical innovations likewise speed recovery and prolong life, each example showing a clear link between the innovation and an enhanced quality of life.

questions.topic: Impact on society of emerging technologies
questions.q:
The images show some examples of the application of emerging technologies: 3D printing (a medical prosthetic leg), biometrics (a security fingerprint scan), nanotechnology (a health smart watch) and a smart card (an Opal travel card).

Analyse the potential impact of emerging technologies on society.

Your answer will be assessed on how well you: demonstrate knowledge and understanding relevant to the question; communicate ideas and information using relevant examples; and present a sustained, logical and cohesive response.

criteria.descriptor: Shows a comprehensive understanding of the potential impact of emerging technologies on society; draws out and relates implications of the potential impact; communicates using relevant examples; responds in a sustained, logical and cohesive manner
Explains the potential impact of emerging technologies on society; communicates using relevant examples; responds in a logical manner
Describes the potential impact of emerging technologies on society; may include a relevant example
Outlines the potential impact of emerging technologies including a link to society
Shows a limited understanding of emerging technologies

questions.modelAnswer: Emerging technologies developed to meet real needs will continue to change and improve quality of life. 3D printing of a prosthetic leg produces a more aesthetically pleasing, customised replacement with a short concept-to-market lead time, improving the user's mobility, independence and self-esteem. Biometrics such as fingerprint scanning vastly improve security by identifying individuals, and will expand to DNA, eye and voice recognition to help create a safer world and reduce identity theft. Nanotechnology in smart watches enables compact, multifunction products with real-time data reporting, encouraging society to monitor and take responsibility for its own health and fitness. Smart cards like the Opal card make travel payment faster and more convenient and help shift towards a cashless society, though they raise concerns over personal data security and can disadvantage older or remote users with limited access to technology. Overall, acceptance of these technologies will keep growing out of need, making life easier, quicker and more convenient while bringing new security and equity implications that society must manage.
